title: Sprint 3 preflight & access walkthrough
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on access handoff and preflight checklist for Sprint 3. Confirmed staging credentials, discussed VPC peering options and telemetry instrumentation. SE explained KV cache warmup and batching tweaks to address tail latency noted in last run. Security asked for KMS keyflow diagram and SOC2/ISO references. Agreed next steps: 6-hour stress run with increased sampling, enable tracing on 2 endpoints, and handoff of jumpbox credentials by 7/13.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-11
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (StratusPay Head of ML), Ethan Ross (Infra), Priya Sharma (Security)

Summary: quick preflight for Sprint 3 onboarding; focus on access, perf run, tracing and security handover.

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate, uh, squeezing this in. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya Singh: Maya here, hi.
[00:10] Ethan Ross: Ethan, on infra.
[00:12] Priya Sharma: Priya from security.
[00:14] Diego Martinez: Diego, Redwood SE.
[00:16] Ava Chen: Cool. We planned to go through the preflight checklist, confirm the staging gateway creds, and then dig into the latency tail we saw in last night's run.

[00:32] Maya Singh: Yep that sounds good. We did provision the staging subnet and we have the service account ready but we hit a snag with the jumpbox keys yesterday.
[00:40] Ethan Ross: Right; I regenerated the keypair this morning, I put the public key into the inbound rules but we need the Redwood ssh fingerprint to add to the known hosts. I put a note in the shared doc.
[00:49] Ava Chen: Great — Ethan can you paste that in the chat after? we need it for the gateway handoff. Also we'll need the CIDR block for the peering, so Diego can set up the route.

[00:58] Ethan Ross: Yep will do.

[01:02] Diego Martinez: On the infra side, quick note: for the warmup we recommend a 30 minute KV cache priming, then a batch replay for the top 10 request patterns. We saw a big gap in tail latency likely from cold KV misses.
[01:18] Priya Sharma: When you say KV cash — is that like our Redis layer? How are you handling keys? This is a data residency concern.
[01:24] Diego Martinez: Ah, sorry transcription, K-V cache — that's the model key-value attention cache inside the runtime, not customer Redis. We do not persist user inputs there; it's ephemeral in memory. I can send a diagram.
[01:36] Priya Sharma: Okay that helps, please include lifecycle and clarifications on retention. We also need to see KMS integration details — who holds the key, where is it stored, any HSM tie-in.
[01:45] Ava Chen: We'll attach the KMS flow and the SOC2 evidence summary to the security pack. Priya we'll make sure the HSM integration notes are explicit.

[01:52] Maya Singh: About the latency: last night the 99.9th p95 jumped for sequences around 1.2k tokens — is that because of batching or kernel selection?
[02:02] Diego Martinez: Likely both. On longer sequences the kernel dispatch is different and batching can mix short and long which causes head-of-queue issues. Two mitigations: set sequence-aware batching (so only similar seq lens batch together) and enforce a small max batch for >512 tokens. We also recommend a quantized variant for non-critical endpoints to reduce tail.
[02:20] Ethan Ross: If we do quantized models are we losing quality for our chat summarization?
[02:24] Diego Martinez: There's a small delta — usually acceptable for classification or embeddings. For generative summaries we can A/B test; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per route.

[02:38] Maya Singh: Can Redwood do a canary? We want fallback if the quantized route underperforms.
[02:43] Ava Chen: Yep — canary + automatic fallback is supported. You can route 5% to quantized, monitor quality metrics, then roll back if regressions hit the threshold. We'll show the rollout config.

[02:55] Priya Sharma: On authentication — we need SSO and SAML. Are you supporting IdP initiated flows or just SP? Also what's the RBAC model?
[03:04] Diego Martinez: We support both IdP and SP, standard S-A-M-L 2.0 flows. For RBAC we have org -> project -> token scope; tokens can be scoped to a model or route. Admins can set read/write and network egress policies.

[03:18] Priya Sharma: Ok can you send the SSO integration doc and sample metadata?
[03:22] Ava Chen: Sure, will attach. Also we need to confirm audit log retention — how long do you want request-level logs retained?
[03:30] Priya Sharma: For now 90 days, but if we go enterprise we might need 365. Depends on cost.

[03:36] Diego Martinez: Noted. We can tier logs; high-fidelity for 90 days, low res for longer.

[03:42] Maya Singh: Going back to the perf run — what exact script do you want us to run in staging? Last time we used the synthetic generator but the shape didn't match prod.
[03:50] Ava Chen: Good point. We'll send a templated runner that replays a sampled request set from your prod trace (anonymized) so distribution matches. The plan: 6-hour run with ramp to 70% qps and two 1-hour steady-state windows. Diego will collect traces and us analyze tail.

[04:07] Diego Martinez: For tracing, please enable verbose spans on /generate and /chat and keep sampling at 100% for first 20 minutes then 10% after. That helps pinpoint kernel switch points.

[04:18] Ethan Ross: That will add overhead, we need to ensure the agents don't saturate the network, I'll carve out 20 Mbps for the host.

[04:25] Priya Sharma: And encryption in transit — TLS 1.2 or 1.3? We require 1.3 where possible.
[04:29] Diego Martinez: We support TLS 1.3. Also mTLS for private deployments if you prefer.

[04:36] Maya Singh: How about observability dashboards — can we get per-route token cost breakdown?
[04:40] Ava Chen: Yes, Redwood Console will show token-level cost, latency percentiles per route, and can export to your DataDog/Prometheus via the exporter. We'll drop the dashboard templates in the shared folder.

[04:49] Maya Singh: Anything else on infra?
[04:51] Ethan Ross: Just firewall rules: outbound to redwood endpoints on 443 and the peering route. Also confirm we don't need extra ports for the jumpbox.

[04:58] Diego Martinez: No extra ports. SSH over 22 for the jumpbox is fine; gateway talks over 443. We'll provide fingerprint.

[05:05] Priya Sharma: Security pack — what specifically will you include? We need SOC2 Type II summary, ISO statement, pen test high-level, KMS flow, SAML metadata, and contact for infra incidents.
[05:15] Ava Chen: We'll include all that plus a runbook for incidents and contact SLAs.

[05:20] Maya Singh: Ok great. For rollout — after the 6-hour run if tail looks stable we want to start canarying 2% traffic to prod for one day. Is that fine?

[05:26] Diego Martinez: Yep, and we can configure auto-fallback if error rate or conv-quality drops beyond your threshold. We'll want the quality eval set to be the same human-graded prompts for the canary.

[05:35] Ava Chen: Quick recap and ownership: Ava will send perf-run script and security pack by 7/13. Diego will enable tracing, run cache warmup and share logs. Ethan will supply CIDR and jumpbox known-hosts. Priya to confirm audit retention.

[05:50] Maya Singh: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[05:52] Priya Sharma: Only waiting on KMS diagram and assurance around HSM if needed.
[05:55] Ava Chen: We'll prioritize that.

[05:58] Diego Martinez: One small note: if you see repeat 502s in the tail that's usually a kernel OOM in the model path; bumping burst capacity or smaller batch caps helps.
[06:07] Ethan Ross: We'll watch for 502s. I'll also run the NAT gateway throughput check pre-run.

[06:13] Ava Chen: Okay last call — schedule the stress run? We aiming for Wed 7/15 02:00 UTC?
[06:18] Maya Singh: That time works for us.
[06:20] Ava Chen: Perfect. I'll send calendar invite and notes. Thanks everyone.
[06:24] Meeting end.

Notes/Links: shared drive link: https://redwood.example.com/shared/stratuspay/poc/sprint3
Security pack placeholder: link to S3/drive (will be uploaded 7/13)
Perf run template: https://redwood.example.com/tools/perf-run-template

Transcription notes: some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (K-V cache vs KV cache, S-A-M-L), speaker overlaps occasionally labeled as single speaker.
